title: Coroner's jury wants Tasers for police
article: A coroner's jury recommended that all front-line police officers in Ontario be equipped with and trained in the use of Taser stun guns.

The jury of three men and two women also determined that Peter Lamonday, a 33-year-old landscaper from London, Ont., died of a cocaine induced excited delirium on May 14, 2004. He died after London police shocked him with the 50,000-volt weapon.
London deputy Police Chief Tony McGowan said the recommendation on expanded Taser use goes further than the province and police have so far.
Seven London police officers were cleared in Lamonday's death last August by the provincial Special Investigations Unit, Ontario's police watchdog.
